selected_evidence.requirement: Encrypted volume created and mounted at /srv/secure
selected_evidence.summary: cryptsetup luksFormat succeeded on the file-backed image, luksOpen succeeded creating /dev/mapper/secure_srv, ext4 was created and mounted at /srv/secure with a test file written and read back.

selected_evidence.requirement: Volume unlocks and mounts on its own at boot (pre-reboot proof of mechanism)
selected_evidence.summary: Added crypttab entry referencing the keyfile and fstab entry for the mapper device; systemd generated systemd-cryptsetup@secure_srv.service and srv-secure.mount and pulled srv-secure.mount into local-fs.target automatically (no noauto/manual enable needed); manually starting the unit unlocked and mounted the volume successfully, proving the boot path works.
Captured pre-restart boot_id (f9bf293d-1eb8-423e-b185-84e94db646f3), machine-id, uptime, and confirmed srv-secure.mount active with data present, as the baseline for node1 (the only managed node).

Issued a backgrounded systemctl reboot that returned an acknowledgement before the node disconnected; the immediate follow-up exec confirmed the node was down (connection reset), proving the reboot actually occurred.

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 changed boot identity after restart
selected_evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id read as e7733aa3-693a-4ae6-82d3-1fce6038a1db (different from the pre-restart f9bf293d-...) with a fresh uptime timestamp, proving a genuine restart rather than a service bounce.

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 post-restart recovery of encrypted volume and data
selected_evidence.summary: After the restart, systemd-cryptsetup@secure_srv.service completed successfully with no manual action, srv-secure.mount is active, /srv/secure is mounted from /dev/mapper/secure_srv, and the pre-existing test file content ('hello') was read back intact, confirming automatic unlock, mount, and data integrity survive a reboot.
